evidence_found.what: Independent Auditor's Examination Report on Restated Consolidated Financial Information, jointly issued by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP and Chaturvedi & Shah LLP, dated 7 October 2026 (UDINs 26100459QBZXUZ8355 / 26122179ZKMPTF3256).

Full examination-report text: no going-concern paragraph, no 'material uncertainty related to going concern', no emphasis-of-matter paragraph, no adverse/disclaimer language; para 8 opinion unmodified.

Verbatim: 'Our opinion on the Special Purpose Interim Consolidated Financial Statements and Consolidated Financial Statements is not modified in respect of above matters with respect to our reliance on work done and the reports of the other auditors...'
evidence_found.use: Modified-opinion absence is not going-concern absence (A19).

evidence_found.what: Note 47.4 'Non-adjusting events': (a) 'There are no audit qualification in auditor's report for the financial period / year ended 30th June, 2026, 30th June, 2025, 31st March, 2026, 31st March, 2025 and 31st March, 2024 which require adjustments.'; (b) 'There are no matters reported with respect to Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements in auditor's report for [the same five periods]'; (c) 'There are no Emphasis of matters in auditor's report for the period / year ended 30th June, 2026, 30th June, 2025, 31st March, 2026, 31st March, 2025 and 31st March, 2024.'
evidence_found.use: NEW this pass: a scoped, five-period negative about qualifications, other legal/regulatory matters and EOM in the auditor's reports. It is silent on going concern, and it is in the notes, not the auditor's report.

evidence_found.what: The only occurrence of the phrase 'going concern' in all 591 pages: '...all assets and liabilities of the optic fibre cable undertaking of RJIL stood transferred to and vested with JDFPL, at their carrying values, on a going concern basis with effect from March 31, 2019...' (Composite Scheme of Arrangement narrative).
evidence_found.use: Accounting basis of a 2019 scheme transfer — not auditor uncertainty. Not evidence either way.

evidence_found.what: The examination report relies on the auditors' reports dated 7 October 2026 (interim), 24 April 2026, 24 April 2025 and 22 April 2024 for the underlying consolidated financial statements. Those underlying reports are NOT reproduced in the filing.
evidence_found.use: The documents that would carry an SA 570 material-uncertainty paragraph are referenced but absent from the retained corpus.

evidence_not_found: 'material uncertainty related to going concern' — 0 occurrences in 591 pages
'significant doubt' / 'ability to continue as a going concern' — 0 occurrences
'no material uncertainty' / negated uncertainty — 0 occurrences (so the engine's polarity guard was never even reached)
the underlying statutory audit reports on the Consolidated Financial Statements for FY2024, FY2025, FY2026 and the June 2026 interim period
any management or director going-concern assertion

technical_findings.assessment: No evidence was lost between source and canonical input. The field is absent because no qualifying statement exists in the filing and A19 forbids deriving a negative from an unmodified opinion, from silence, or from a negated statement.

classification: SEMANTIC / GOVERNANCE (A19 negative-confirmation rule deferred). Not factual-missing in the ordinary sense: the filing is silent, and the reports that could speak are not in the corpus. Not technical.
justification: A19 (approved) requires UNKNOWN in exactly this state, and the critical_data list converts the missing flag into INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than a favourable verdict. The recorded disposition is correct under the governing rule.
minimum_evidence_to_resolve_factually: The statutory auditor's report(s) on the Consolidated Financial Statements for FY2026 (and the June 2026 interim statements), showing whether an SA 570 material-uncertainty section exists; or
an auditor confirmation scoped to going concern covering the same periods
both would be source evidence, not a rule change; either would set the field only if it contained positive uncertainty language

governance_question.note: A19 already answers the question and explicitly defers the negative rule. Re-opening it requires A19's four prerequisites: (1) evidence-coverage definition, (2) required-language specification, (3) false-negative measurement on filings that DO carry a paragraph, (4) re-score decision for historical records.
governance_question.narrowed_question_this_pass: If Ramki ever revisits it, the question is now sharper than 'silence': would note 47.4 (a)+(b)+(c) — an explicit, five-period negative for audit qualifications, other legal/regulatory matters and Emphasis of Matter — together with the examination report's silence, be accepted as a negative confirmation of going-concern uncertainty? A19's text says an unmodified opinion alone may not; it does not address this broader scoped negative.
governance_question.why_not_auto_accepted: An SA 570 material-uncertainty section is not a qualification and not an Emphasis of Matter, so a 'no qualification / no EOM' statement is logically silent on going concern. Accepting it would be a new rule with a false-negative boundary.

recommended_next_action: No action that changes the record. Optionally obtain the underlying auditor's reports (external evidence) in a later pass; otherwise leave K1 UNVERIFIED.
